utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I would like to greet everyone here in this courtroom on this 23rd of May. Good morning to Mr. Kruger, to the Defence counsel, to the accused, and to everyone else in this courtroom. I'd like to ask the registrar for us to move into private session for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in -- we are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll have the witness brought in. As for time now. I've been told that Mr. Karnavas has been granted some time by other Defence counsel. Is that the case, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President; good morning, Your Honours; good morning everyone else. Yes. I am told that I have approximately 30 minutes left from my own time. In addition to that, I've been given 20 minutes from the Coric team, 15 minutes from the Petkovic team, and 10 or 15 minutes from the Pusic team, and I think that may be sufficient for me to -- to cover all the things I need to cover. We will be much more efficient today, hopefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you know, we are now going to proceed with the cross-examination. I am now giving the floor to Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to pick up where we left off yesterday, and if we could look at 1D 01530. Could we provide the documents to the witness. Thank you. This is 1D 01530, 1530. This is still on that chapter we were talking about yesterday with respect to --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Good. Now, as we could see from the top, there's a date, April 6, 1994. In reference -- if we go to Article 1, we can see the date of 18 of March, 1994, and in essence for the title of it, it says, "Law on Ratification of The Preliminary Agreement on Establishing of Confederation Between the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Republic of Croatia." ? First question: Did you have an opportunity to see -- to come across this document when you were in country?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this period I was between missions, and I came back after the federation had been formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So -- so the question -- the answer to my question, did you get a chance to look at this document at some point when you were in Bosnia-Herzegovina, "yes," "no," "I don't recall."

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. By the -- by the time -- when you got back did you get a full briefing on what exactly had been agreed upon in Washington, or what was the Washington Agreement about?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, again in broad terms, and I would just remind you that I -- when I went back the second time I began my service in Tapusko in Croatia, so my initial weeks were spent dealing with different issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for reminding me that. Now, if we look at Article 1 under Preliminary Agreement, it's on the first page, so this would be towards the bottom of the page -- or before that in the preamble - yesterday I kept calling it "preambula," because my colleague, Suzana Tomanovic, calls it that in her language. It says, "the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina," in further text, "Federation," and, and "the Republic of Croatia," in further text "Croatia," "have agreed as follows." So from here it would stand that the Federation as opposed to Bosnia-Herzegovina is making an agreement with Croatia; correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That was part of the Washington Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, if we were just for the benefit of the Trial Chamber if we were to -- to look on page 6 there's Annex 2. We see that there is attached an agreement between the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we need not discuss this too much but it would seem at least that this whole notion of a confederation that had been talked about and that the Croats, at least in Bosnia that were talking about, we see some sort of realisation through this document?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a very important component. I think if they were not together, an Croat independent republic on its own, then, as a part of the of the federation forming with the Muslims, it was extremely important to hang on to the component of connection with Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, it was also important for the --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: International community.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. But it was also important for the Muslims, and I keep -- I have to go back to this, to get a port, as opposed to being land-locked, because they needed access to the sea, and this was one way of ensuring that.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if you look at page 4.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you look at page 4, we will see, Your Honours, there's annex 1, "Agreement ensuring for the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina access to the Adriatic through the territory of the Republic of Croatia."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So at least from this agreement we see that access to the sea was an important component.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. The Muslims had access to the sea before and they were going to maintain it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Hold on. Are we talking about Neum?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If one classes that as a port, it was access to the sea, yes; and the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And let me ask you this: Is that a deep water port "yes," "no," "I don't know"?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No it's not a keep water port.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Now, let's turn to the next document. 1D 01539, 1539. And this is just an excerpt from the Balkan Odyssey by David Owen. I believe it's sir David Owen or is it Lord Owen?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lord Owen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So that's even bigger; right?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. We dispensed with those notions in 1776, I believe, we being the Americans.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, your loss, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So -- okay. Now, to your understanding and belief, is Lord Owen a serious individual?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just before we -- I answer that question, I haven't got the document or I can't find the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 39. And if you don't we have an extra copy --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not appear to be in one of these.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. This was something that was added on.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lord Owen, yes, a serious international figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And like Lord Carrington, I believe was at one time --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] He was also the British Foreign Minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Foreign Minister or Defence Minister?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] British Foreign Minister at the time of the Falklands war in 1982.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Okay.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] He resigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would counsel make breaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I was just about to do that. Thank you for that warning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I must caution you that we need to slow down. Now, in your capacity at that period of time, did you have access to Lord Owen?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lord Owen sat at the top of the ECMM reporting chain. I didn't personally have access directly to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So I take it you never discussed with him what at all he was doing when he was with Mr. Vance or later on with Stoltenberg?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, can I assume or can we assume that the ECMM was getting briefed by whatever it was that Lord Owen and Mr. Stoltenberg were doing at the time?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, in broad terms, and I would also comment that probably on the ground we would have liked to have had more information but for instance we knew about the study which he commissioned at Neum.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Study on Neum. That would have been to see whether that --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To see whether it was a deep sea port or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There you go. And the studied turned out to be what?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was a technical study and, as we said, we established that it was not a deep sea port.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And so if you want cargo ships coming in with cargo to Bosnia, that's not the place.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's what that report concluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, there you go. Now, did you by any chance have an opportunity to read Lord Owen's book? It was published afterwards --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't believe I have read that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And sir if I were to -- if I were to -- the very first page, there is this quote from Misha Glenny have you heard of him?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes we've all read Misha Glenny's books prior to deployment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And he starts with, "henceforth nobody can talk authoritatively about the course of this war without engaging this text in detail." Now, obviously you haven't read the text but if Misha Glenny says it, is that something that you would at least consider?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's rather an absolute statement but I would consider that it would be worthwhile we now reading this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, if we turn to the next page and in the book it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At least in this edition, it's page 226, Your Honours. There's a rather lengthy passage, and unfortunately I will have to read it. I believe we did provide copies to the interpreters. I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But I want to read this and then get your understanding because I think yesterday we established, sir, that you -- you did not have all the information at the time from all sides, including the internationals; correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, and I don't think anybody had all the information from all of the sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And, as you put it, and I think this is a truism, "the political situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina could not be seen in isolation from the international peace talks"?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I mean, that's what you said, and I think it's -- it stands to reason that if the internationals are involved, obviously one must look at the international peace talks that are going on as well as what is happening on the ground. Now -- so let's look at what Lord Owen has to say, and I'm going to go to the bottom of the page. And the title of this chapter is, "A Union of Three Republics." We see that on the following page. Now, it says here: "In Geneva on 20 August I briefed EC missions and circulated the documents for a Bosnian settlement to which the leaders of the three parties had agreed in principle. The leaders were going to consult their 'parliaments' and give their final response to the co-chairmen at the meeting in Geneva on 31 August." Notice the quotes, parliaments. I hope that --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed. We may draw a different opinion as to why it's in parentheses [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm just noting it's there and you would suspect that Lord Owen is, is rather precise in language.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm suggesting that he's meaning parliaments, as in perhaps self-styled parliaments, without giving them that particular authority, is the way I would interpret it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. And that, sir -- and that, sir, since you want to volunteer that information, would also go to the parliament, quote-unquote, that exists in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that had a legitimacy at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll have other witnesses talk about the legitimacy and see how many Croats and how many Serbs were functioning and making -- in that particular parliament but we're not here for that. But let's continue. "As co-chairmen, we had warned against trying to make further significant changes to the agreements. We believe that except for Eastern Bosnia, the outcome met all the criteria set by the EC foreign affairs council in June. Including their part of Sarajevo which accounted for two per cent, the Muslims would get 30 per cent of the total territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. All the constitutional principles of the Vance-Owen Plan, for what they were now worth, were some additional points, such as commitments against armies simply being turned into police forces, had been built in the agreements in the form of a complete constitutional instrument. Muslim access to the Sava and Adriatic was guaranteed." Now, see I'm raising my voice, and I'm underscoring it because I want to make sure that we are on the same page, that at least Lord Owen knows and is highlighting that it's the Muslims that want access to the sea, and not something that is being imposed on the Muslims by the internationals?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I would quite interpret it the same way --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- as I discussed yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. "Mostar was to be placed under EC administrative for up to two years along the same lines as UN administration of Sarajevo. Tudjman had been implacably opposed to UN control of Mostar, so I suggested that the EC should take it on, and Tudjman had accepted this across the negotiating table. Fortunately, the EC later backed me. It was agreed that part of the city would operate as the capital of the Croat majority republic." Let me read that again: "It was agreed that part of the city would operate as the capital of the Croat majority republic. On Eastern Bosnia, we were disappointed that we could not negotiate a territorial link between the Muslim areas of the Zepa and Gorazde but this the Serbs fiercely resisted. The best we could achieve was a road link to be maintained and policed by the Muslims. "Central Bosnia was the most difficult part of the negotiations. Here, Boban was finally persuaded to give up Croatian claims of 1 per cent of territory which then went to the Muslims. The tension -- the tension in the area remained high, however, and we feared that further fierce fighting could erupt, particularly around Gornji Vakuf." And I take it -- let me stop here -- let me pause. I take it, giving up that 1 per cent of the territory, which at least the Croats in that area thought should be under Croatian control might have upset the Croatians.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might. I think the paragraph that you've just read brings out some interesting points and sort of explains some of the local colour I was painting yesterday, the issue here of the EC control of Mostar. How did the Croats on the ground feel about that? And that was one of the times when we were instructed to -- to give feedback.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the other element if I just might say would also be the anticipated further fierce fighting which could erupt particularly around Gornji Vakuf, which again would explain my particular interest in what was happening on the Makljen ridge, the movement of the HV forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. All right. And could also further explain why some of the Croats over there felt that they had been abandoned and were actually being forced to leave because at the negotiating table Boban is having to give up 1 per cent of the territory?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. At the meeting on the 31st, the Assembly meeting I went to, this was expressed as I said by with some concern, which those further away from Mostar that they well may be sacrificed in any - I should be careful - negotiated away their position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Negotiated away. And we're not talking about ethnic cleansing or reverse ethnic cleansing. We're talking about trying to find a negotiated settlement where you have three republics within one state; correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct and.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And at no time, sir, at no time at least to your understanding, did anyone -- was anyone at the international scene proposing that there be population exchanges once you formed these republics?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The international community certainly wasn't proposing that. However, I do believe that as part of providing security for ethnic and constituent groups, there was, certainly in the case of the Bosnian Serbs and I do also believe in the case of the Bosnian Croats, a desire to collect people into the area of which they would have territorial integrity of their three republics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Having a desire and negotiating -- having a desire and negotiating at the table for three republics are two different things. And I'm reminded here on the transcript you say HV forces. You mean to say -- at the Makljen ridge, the movement of HV forces. Are you talking about HVO forces or HV forces there?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: HV forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me continue. "Overall I warned the EC that the final outcome was still on a knife's edge. We thought Izetbegovic would give a fair wind to the agreement and other members of the Bosnian Presidency had reacted fairly positively when we briefed them." Who are the other members of the Bosnian Presidency, if you know at the time -- if you know?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would imagine he's talking here about Ejup Ganic, Haris Silajdzic. I wouldn't be able to name any of the Croats or Serbs involved. Those are the names I would assume he means.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were any Serbs or Croats serving on the Bosnian Presidency at that time?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they were, it would have been a very sparse representation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There's no sense in being cute because, you know, I can be very rude in cutting you off. I'm just asking a direct question. Do you know, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ever make any efforts top find out who was on the Presidency, yes, no?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not make efforts to find out who was on the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So: "The areas from which the Serbs were to withdraw on the proposed map amounted to 16.7 per cent of the whole country and 23.9 per cent of the Serb-held territory, significantly less than the VOPP." Then we go on: "The -- the package then faced the same US prevarication which had accompanied the VOPP." Now, do you know what they're talking about the "US prevarication"?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you have an inkling of what that means?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were always differentials in approach between EU and the US on what should happen in Bosnia. The US had a much more interventionist approach. There were issues being discussed about whether various groups or organisations or, in particular, the government itself should have been reinforced. EU had a slightly different perspective to the US.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, prevarication, what does that mean? I mean, do you know the term?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for a dictionary definition --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You can be kind. You can go -- go soft on that?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a determined and set course of action but one of delay and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Obfuscating?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obfuscating.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Less than candid?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Less than truthful?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Dishonest?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think your thesaurus is better than mine. Yes, all those would do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: "Now, their special envoy, Redman, who knew all the twists and turns of the negotiations and seemed personally sympathetic, was working within a remit which appeared to consist of never being wrong-footed into ending up in opposition of the Bosnian Herzegovinian government. The US were adamant that although they were not prepared to pronounce on the details, they would say to the Bosnian -- to the Bosnia-Herzegovina government that the package warranted very serious consideration and that it was the best chance for the moment. The non-aligned movement had a UNSCR at an advance stage before the Security Council which threatened to establish new principles for a settlement. So it became necessary so -- for Stoltenberg to travel to New York and to put the case -- and put the case for the package, which was we had to stress yet again not an Owen-Stoltenberg package but one agreed by the parties negotiated over a tense and difficult month in Geneva." Now, were you aware of this by the way?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Geneva talks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would Mr. Karnavas have a set of documents for the French booth. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We apologise to the French booth. An oversight, not a sleight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we go on, I want to save some time over this, if we could -- we might be able to skip. Let's go to the paragraph where it says: "After 36 hours in which the Serbs and Muslims seemed to be vying with one another to avoid being the first to come out totally in favour or totally against the package, the Bosnian Serbs in their Assembly voted 55 to 14 in favour. The Muslim majority Bosnian parliament, however, voted unanimously only in favour of continuing the negotiations. Izetbegovic said his main problem was the map. He wanted Foca, Bratunac, Visegrad, Prijedor, Kozarac, and Sanski Most, all Muslim towns before the war and all in provinces likely to elect Muslim majority under the VOPP. He also wanted access to the sea at Neum. The Bosnian Croat parliament approved the package with only one vote against." Now, were you aware of this, this drama that was being played out as retold by -- as retold by Lord Owen in his book?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a surprise to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: See, I didn't ask you whether it was a surprise. Had I asked you, are you surprised. I'm asking, were you aware.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were aware of the Geneva talks, but for instance --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you aware of this? I'm speaking concretely about what I just read. I'm not asking for some global picture and I'm not asking for the "we"; I'm asking you, because we -- I don't have the EC as an organisation here, the ECMM. So, were you aware of it? Because you were the one, sir, and this is why I'm pressing you, and I'm not being disrespectful, but I'm pressing because you were making reports. You were drawing conclusions. Others were relying on it, and my whole point to the judges are that, albeit you were very objective in the way you were trying to conduct your business, you were labouring under circumstances that do did not allow you to have access to all the information that perhaps the Judges may need in order to draw the proper conclusion. So my question is: Were you aware, you specifically, aware of what I just read to you, "yes," "no," "maybe," "I don't recall"?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's never such a simple world as that. What I'm saying is, yes, I was aware of Geneva talks and we were broadly aware of what was being discussed but, for instance, I did not know, and you have listed many towns or Lord Owen has here, of the detail. So you're right, we did not have all the details, but I knew of the talks and I knew broadly of what was trying to be achieved at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But did you know the positions that were being taken by the various parties? Yes or no? I mean, it's a very concrete --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in -- not exactly, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And it's rather clear, sir, and believe me, I think that when I read all of this, it's very clear. I think neighbour who reads your reports sees a very serious individual who is trying to be somebody I have. I give you that. But I'm trying to point out that perhaps he didn't have all the facts at the time, and you agree with me on that; right?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I would say that was a statement of the obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I didn't have all the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you know that -- did you know about parliamentary sessions being held in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's move on to the next area and just have some quick documents. I want to focus on P 05709. This was generated by Martin Garrod, and I believe he's a sir. It's Sir Martin Garrod; right?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, and I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And did you -- did you know him or know of him?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him. I knew him well. When he first deployed, he came into my team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And, as I understand, he's an extremely serious individual?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a British monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, what does that mean? My question was that he's a serious individual. Being a British monitor doesn't mean anything to me. He is serious or non-serious, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, he writes at the bottom of the -- at the bottom of the second paragraph, and this is about a conversation that he's having with, I believe, Mr. Hadzihasanovic -- did you know who Mr. Hadzihasanovic was, Mr. Enver Hadzihasanovic commander of the 3rd BiH Corps?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew Mr. Hadzihasanovic well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, you met him?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay now here he's talking - I don't want to go into the whole part of this because the Judges will have it and can read it at their leisure, and will point out relevant passages - but at the very bottom, he says, Hadzihasanovic is saying, that he added that there was something that Europe had not noticed: "He gave the Croats and Serbs who lived in Bosnia -- he says "who gave" - who gave - "the Croats and Serbs who lived in Bosnia to call themselves Croats and Serbs? They are merely Roman Catholic Bosnians or Orthodox Bosnians." Now, were you aware that he is subscribed to such notions that there weren't Serbs or Croats in Bosnia who were indigenous as a constituent peoples, but, rather, they were all Bosnian of a different religion?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was often articulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I knew that he had these views.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And at that point in time, at least at some other point in time, he was a pretty high-level officer, was he not?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a corps commander and is of interest to this Court, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we just look very briefly on -- on paragraph 4. This is something again slightly different. Here, Sir Martin Garrod says, and I'm just read part of the paragraph, he says: "It was difficult, for example, to persuade people that they should provide access and freedom of movement when they see little practical results from our efforts." This is what Hadzihasanovic is saying. "In addition, instances of smuggling and 'criminal activity' (by international agencies)," that's in parentheses, "led to the roadblocks." Now, yesterday or Monday I believe you did in fact indicate that the Muslims were also blocking the roads at times; correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, do you know what he's talking about, the international agencies smuggling and being involved in criminal activity what is exactly he talking about? Because I would assume that ECMM being one of the international agencies, that accusation in part may have -- may be being lodged against yourselves as well. Any idea?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was a regular allegation, not just from the Muslims but it was, for instance, claims and I do believe on occasions established facts that some aid convoys were carrying more than just aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This was an established fact. When you say, "carrying more than aid," you mean like carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were, I believe, times when, yes, carrying arms and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right and that accusation was also being lodged that the Muslims were doing that in their aid convoys?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that the international community had been carrying more than humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And allegations were made by both Muslims against the international community, Croats against the international community, and Serbs, that that was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And was that in fact happening, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do believe that there were a couple of times when it was established but it was -- it was rare but I do believe it was established a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, if we go to paragraph 10, just very quickly, I'm just go to look at part of it, it says here that, "He made clear that elements of the BiH at least have the will and capacity to continue the fight until they achieve their goals. He also implied that money was not a problem," in quotes -- I mean, in parentheses, "(with donations coming from abroad)," end of parentheses, "and if he is expressing Izetbegovic's views, peace is a long way off." Now, were you aware that Sir Martin Garrod was commenting about the views being held by Hadzihasanovic at this period of time in such a fashion? That -- we're talking about 7 October 1993. That would have been a time when you were going into Mostar?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7th of October. No, I was still actually up as head of CC Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you were about -- I think it was the middle of October that you made it to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two weeks after that, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, were you aware -- did you ever access to this particular document?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would have been in the same headquarters as him --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When he's talking about "their goals," do you know exactly what he means by "their goals?" Would access to the sea be one of them?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Primarily the goals articulated to us was the maintenance of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the internationally recognised state.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. As a unitary state?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a unitary state.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where it's one person, one vote, and then the Catholic -- the Catholics and the Orthodox would be one peoples?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was the -- maintenance of the state which had been accepted and ratified by the UN, which was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. I think we got the point. If we go to the next document, there are two documents that I want to talk about in particular. Yesterday, you were shown one document where we talked about -- and this was the document that I shared with you was 2790. 2790, and I made reference -- 7290, and that's where I made reference to a Safet, the an armija staff officer of the 4th Corps who stated that Muslims were not ready for peace until they had access to the sea and so on. And I asked you who Safet was and you weren't quite sure. Could that be Safet Cibo, C-i-b-o?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be. I haven't actually found the document, but I do remember what you're saying, so it could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Have you ever met Mr. Safet Cibo?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name certainly rings a bell, but I -- I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, the document that I want to go to is -- that was by way of reference. Now, the document is 6511. 6511. And if we look under political and this is dated 5 November 1993 this would have been at the time you were in the Mostar area. Do you have the document, sir?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not if it's from your file.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Yes I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It would have been -- I apologise. And this was something that was shown to you incidentally by the Prosecutor as the previous one, although they omitted to point out those references.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And if we look at the section under Political, and I think this is something that is rather curious and perhaps even telling. It says, "M1 met Safet Cibo, president of the War Presidency who had recently returned from Sarajevo." And then there is some parentheses some letters and numbers. "Cibo said he was pleased with the new government led by Silajdzic as it represented the first real Bosnian government. He anticipated more changes shortly." Now, who is M1?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the team that reported to me, and it was based in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, having read that, do you recall meeting Mr. Cibo now, the president of the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. Mike 1 isn't me, but I may well have met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it is a very interesting paragraph, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Since these were your team members, and obviously the information is coming to you, do you know whether at the time, reading this, you asked M1 to explain what exactly Mr. Cibo meant when he said "real," "first real Bosnian government"? What did he meant by that? And if you don't have the answer, we can move on.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the answer, and given hindsight I would probably have pursued that bit more vigorously. It is very interesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Now, let me just go -- share with you one other document that were being -- that was circulated at the time and it's 1D 01434. This was being circulated, I am told, in Central Bosnia during the war in 1993, and --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. It reads -- it starts with: "In the name of Allah, the most gracious. Muslim brethren the time has finally come to liberate our homeland. Like 500 years ago, the Muslim Corps will rule over its historic areas. "We have had enough of injustice both from the kris/cross Orthodox use and from the kriz/cross Catholic use. Our holy mission is to liberate Mostar and Stolac, Sarajevo, Zvornik, Gorazde, Banja Luka, Doboj, Foca, Nevesinje, Trebinje, and other towns throughout our proud Bosnia will once again embark upon the path of Islam. "Let everyone be aware that Muslims die with the name of Allah on their lips and for the glory of their faith. "We were never stronger. Muslims of the world are with us. "We will take our part of the Adriatic coast. Ploce will be the first Bosnian port and Neum will be the new Constantinople. "This will be our Bosnia and Herzegovina." Incidently, where is Ploce?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ploce is a port in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Had you come --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Karnavas, could you be so kind as to enlighten the Chamber about the origins of this paper, which has no date, no signature, and may be a leaflet distributed by any fanatic somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, that's the whole point. Thank you for that question, and I anticipated you raising it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you for that question, and I anticipated you raising it. This was a leaflet that was being circulated. Whether it was by fanatics, whether this was sanctioned by the government, I don't know. We do know that Mujahedin were running around. But this is something that my colleague, Ms. Suzana Tomanovic, gave me, who was in Doboj throughout the war, and this is where this document came from. So I'm not saying that this was being circulated by the Sarajevo government, but nonetheless, this is the sort of rhetoric that's going around.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And my question to you, sir, is, were you aware that pamphlets, such as this one, were being circulated at the time?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware. I met some of the extremists, including external Mujahedin and the involvement of external elements, finance coming from overseas was something which was of interest particularly during my second tour and under the French Presidency. And I wrote a special report at the time on the influence of Mujahedin in Central Bosnia. And if it helps the Court in a perspective, there certainly were Mujahedin there, and there were certainly very highly motivated indigenous brigades, such as 17 Muslim Brigade, where you had more extreme elements being articulated such as this. It wasn't mainstream at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now we're going to move on very quickly to another -- other sets of documents, and before I do so the term "okruzi"? Okruzi, I think I'm pronouncing it right, did that ever come -- did you ever hear of that term, "okruzi"? You have a phenomenal memory but I wouldn't expect you to remember, but --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. If we could look at 6590. 6590. And this is a document date -- this is in the Prosecution's binder. I'm sorry. The next few documents are from the Prosecutor's binder.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And perhaps you can elucidate a little bit on some of this. I'm still trying to figure it out. Dated 11 November 1993, under the section, Political, it says: "HCC met Smail Karalic, president of the War Presidency Mostar, Ibrahim Kaluda (BiH minister for co-ord Mostar), and Rusmir Cisic (president of the county of Mostar)," and then it goes on to say, "after discussions concerning the delivery of aid (in which EC was accused of -- of implementing a food as well as an arms embargo) HCC addressed the," quote, "county government," unquote, "structure and its aims. Cisic said Mostar county had recently formed (7 November 1993) in Mostar and had authority over the municipalities of Stolac, Capljina, Mostar, Jablanica, Konjic." Question: What is he talking about when he says "Mostar county"? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can see that we were very interested to understand what new structures were emerging. We'd first come across the county structure in Central Bosnia, and my interest was obviously taken with me to Mostar and here you can see I am trying to find out what this county government means, and again I've used parentheses in the same way we described earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And he's explaining a new civilian structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, he's talking about a structure, but then if you go to the assessment, because there's precious little information that I suspect you were able to drag out of them in order to come up with your assessment, it says here --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On paragraph number 7, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, sir, "The meeting in Mostar with the civil authorities provided more important information about the Muslim county level of government. It confirms the primary area -- the primary aim is to develop the humanitarian links and the infrastructure." Then it goes on. "Despite Ciric's statement that Mostar has nothing to trade with the county has one major asset, namely hydroelectric power." Now, I'm trying to figure this out. When you go back, Mostar county incorporates various municipalities; correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And do you know whether there was any legislation that was set up? And I'm talking about legal -- legally, that would be, that would set -- that would allow for the formation of a county or a region or a canton? Because when we look at the size of these municipalities and the geographical area that they would compass, we're talking about a fairly significant chunk of the territory; right?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So question: Did you by any chance ask for or did they ever share with you any documentation that would allow the formation of counties in a constitutional -- within a constitutional framework?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not provide me with any paperwork. You could see I'm probing for as much information as I can get about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And -- one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I may -- if I may just -- if I may profit from the interval. Witness, you speak in the last paragraph in the Assessment of someone spelled Ciric, whereas on the first page you speak repeatedly of someone called Cisic. Do we have a misprint on the last page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I believe we do. I don't remember there being another individual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, for -- I have other documents on this, but since we have that information, we can go to the very last document in this chapter of my cross, which would be 1D 01531, 1531. And that would be in my documents. When it's a D number, you're almost certain to find it in my documents. When it's a P, which means Prosecutor, it will be in their documents. I apologise for not making that clear.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, here we see something that is dated -- at the top we see 6 April 1994, and we see this has been generated as of -- as a result of a session that was held on 30 March 1994. It's a decision to relieve of duties and elect the president of the War Presidency of the municipality of Mostar and the election of the president of Presidency of the Mostar district. Now, if we go to III, we see that, "Smail Klaric is hereby elected as president of the Presidency of the Mostar district." Now, if we go back -- if we look at the original language, we see Okruga [phoen] Mostar. Now we're talking about a district whether it's a county district. Do you know -- have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just need a little bit more help on orientation of the document because although I have --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if you go to -- here we see that "I," "Smail Klaric is hereby relieved of his duties as president --"

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. He's relieved of his duties as president of the War Presidency of the municipality of Mostar. He's replaced, and then we see now he's being elected to the president to the Presidency of the Mostar district. And at the -- and this is -- and -- and of course is this -- does this pre-date or post-date the Washington Agreement?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It post-dates, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So here we already have a Washington Agreement. In here, we see that Izetbegovic as the president of the presidency is appointed someone as part of the Mostar district. Okay? Now, was there a Mostar district at that point in time? If you know; if you don't know, that's fine. We'll save it for another witness.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Now, a couple of housekeeping matters and then I think we're just about done. If we could go to -- I want to -- yesterday you were shown a document by the Prosecutor, and the document that you were shown, and this would be in their binder but this was 7372, but the essence of it is, the essence of it is that -- that you had put down that Boban had stated that, "If the Muslims and Serbs did not accept the union of republics then CRHB would join Croatia." Remember you saying that, that he was up there on his feet making an impassioned plea, this is -- the document is dated 29 December 1993. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I have the document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, first of all, I -- I haven't come across any document where Dr. Jadranko Prlic ever made any statements of that sort.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it since I haven't come across any documents, it's because he never made any such statements.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did once make a statement which I wasn't able to draw a clear conclusion of, but he said some -- if they failed, then we are clear about what we are going to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to share with you the following day, 30th December 1993, and this is 7405. This is a document that was again show to you, and I take it my good friend on the other side simply was in a rush to get through his -- his case and failed to bring this out but in fairness, in context, I think we should. If we look at the it second paragraph under the Political section on page 1.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And this is -- again, this is an ECMM document; correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I wrote it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You wrote it. Okay. Now, here in the middle of the paragraph you say: "With reference to the CRHB Assembly of yesterday, Markovic said the prospect of CRHB joining Croatia in the event of Serbs or Muslims not accepting a union of republics was not a policy decision of the Assembly." "Was not a policy decision of the Assembly." So here you have a different position taken by Mr. Markovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You do. It would suggest that the decision would not be with the Assembly; it would be elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, that's one way of looking at it. The other way of looking at it is, Boban was merely speaking.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be an alternative perspective.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. That's what I'm looking at for fairness, objectively. So also give me the alternative plausible explanation that I'm due, as opposed to giving me one version which, with all due respect, is just one version, one side of the coin. There's another side to that coin, but, very well, we can move on to the next issue.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would hope that you would see from the two reports that I do give both those perspectives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand that but that wasn't drawn out yesterday. That's why I'm bringing it to everyone's attention and to Their Honours, because I suspect that there was a reason why the Prosecution highlighted Boban and omitted Markovic. Of course, that may be for closing argument. Who knows. Okay. If we go on to the next section, and this deals with refugees. I want to focus your attention just very briefly to one document, and it's a Prosecution document. It's P 05960. 5960. And hopefully you can find it with ease. In this particular document, we see --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. For some reason I don't have 60.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps it will be in mine. If not -- it's in my binder, even though -- see, I -- apparently this was a document that was -- been introduced through other witnesses. I apologise --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not trying to confuse you. It says here at the very first -- this was generated on 26 October 1993, if we look at the third page. And if we go back to the first page, it's a report from the trip to Istria in connection to the escort and accommodation of the Croats from Central Bosnia, Kakanj, and Zenica. Now, it says here: "On 20 October 1993 there arrived in Stolac an organised convoy transporting about 6.000 displaced Croats from Kakanj and Zenica who had been temporarily accommodated in Vares." Were you aware of that sir, more or less?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're going to skip and I want to go to the next paragraph, but I wanted to ask you, do you know -- did you know at the time what the military age was?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military age?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah, for people to serve. You know, the --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would be guessing it would be 17, but that is a guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Until what age?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Would it surprise you that it would have been 60 or 65?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was going to say late 50s but, again, it would have been a guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It could have been as young as 16, depending on where you were, but we're talking the range. That was the range. And were you also aware at the time that everybody was mobilised on all three sides, Serbs, Croats, Muslims?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And so that might account for somebody who's being of military age, a male of military age why perhaps those individuals might -- might be of specific significance.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they certainly were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Because obviously if you're in the middle of a war, you want your military-aged men to be fighting or engaged in civil protection matters; correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, of course, were you also aware that this was compulsory? In other words, you couldn't just pass? There were no conscientious objectives, you know, in the sense that, you know, you'll pass out this war?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I was aware that there wasn't much individual discretion allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we go to the next paragraph, Your Honours. "After the men liable for military service were removed from the vehicles and the vehicles were filled with fuel in Celjevo, and after lists of 1.500 displaced persons were created at the border crossing Doljani and Metkovic, we headed as part of the convoy towards Ploce ... two ships (Istra and Liburnija)," I guess I'm killing the name, but, "were waiting to be boarded."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, couple of questions. Here we can see that at least the men of military age, albeit they are being -- they are being displaced from another part, are being separated presumably so they can continue to serve their military duties; correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could draw that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Can we also draw this conclusion, and this may be helpful to our Trial Bench, that those displaced persons now, the remaining displaced persons, are being taken to Croatia and not being repopulated in areas in Herzegovina because they wanted -- this was some sort of a population engineering process, if I could put it in those terms?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the indication from this particular destination of the displaced persons separated, but I visited camps in --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] I understand that you visited camps --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- to try --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] But I --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Yeah, you're right in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I'm also right, am I not, that the picture is rather complex?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I really cannot stand any more. Please slow down. Don't torture the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Give me time. Give me a lever and I'll move the world, as Archimedes said, but without that time, without that lever ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, and if we go very briefly to the third page, just very briefly, in the middle of the page there's the second paragraph. It talks about the 25th October 1993, and we see some figures there. It says, "We return from, I dare say, a job very well done. This part of the evacuation, reception, and accommodation of the displaced Croats from Kakanj and Zenica was conducted on a high level. We agreed with the most responsible people from the RH government on the dynamism and location of the new 3.000 displaced Croats from the Central Bosnia while the first group of 600 displaced Croats from Kakanj will be received and accommodated in the Klana barracks near Rijeka which was renovated by the Italian government." Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay f we go to the next document, and this is a P document, so that would be in your Prosecution binder, and this is 7286, but the point that I was trying -- while you're looking for that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The point for Their Honours is that here we have proof that Croats were being displace the are being taken to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you were shown this document 7286, and you were focused on one part on the front page in the Political section, and when came to one sentence which I thought you might even want to go in and comment on, because I -- I knew that my friend probably had no interest in it, you didn't, so I'm having to spend some time on this. Third paragraph, last sentence. It says: "The difficulties for BiH are magnified due to many Muslim POWs choosing to go abroad rather than return to BiH territory." Okay? So this whole paragraph talks about the exchange problems and the difficulties between civilians and soldiers, but here we have somebody commenting, I don't know if you wrote this, 21 December 1993.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Mike 3, so it wasn't me who met them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know what he means by that?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Or what he meant by that?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to the third paragraph. Sorry, I just wanted to be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm referring to the third paragraph and I'm referring to the last sentence, the sentence which was not read with the rest of the paragraph yesterday when this was pointed out to you and which I think might be of interest. Could you explain to us what you meant when you wrote: "The difficulties for BiH are magnified due to many Muslim POWs choosing to go abroad rather than return to BiH territory," keeping in mind my earlier question having to do with military-age men, compulsory service, and so on and so forth. I think you get my drift?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, and I'm quite clear what I mean here. It was an issue that when there were releases of prisoners, the Muslims very much wanted the prisoners coming out of the camps to come into BiH territory. I think it sent -- for them they told us that it sent very bad signals when people released didn't want to come back and defend and fight for them but wanted to go elsewhere, and that's what I meant by this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My very last topic, sir, has to do with your comments with respect to Anto Valenta. First and foremost, let's get this out of the way, you never heard my client talk about population exchanges?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay and you never heard my client, and I didn't see anywhere in the documents that you or anyone generated, that Dr. Jadranko Prlic ever said that he subscribed to anything that might have been expressed or written by Mr. Valenta?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Mr. Valenta --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- was his deputy at one stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand that, but here we're going to go into -- I just wanted to get that out of the way first and you did not hear Dr. Jadranko Prlic ever say that this was a policy, Anto Valenta's thoughts, philosophy, be it whatever they were, was a policy that had been set in motion?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. As I said yesterday, Dr. Prlic was a -- very practical, pragmatic, and not an ideologue. I never heard him discussing those terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay all right now very quickly and I think this is important for Their Honours, we're going to have the whole book translated, we're going to ask for it to be translated, but, first, let me ask you some preparatory questions did you ever read the book "yes," "no," "I don't recall." The answer is no?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which took sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: His book Anto Valenta's book?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not read that book.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay did you ever have anybody read it to you?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good grief, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay I see now before we go into that some -- you know, have you ever heard of the Islamic Declaration that was written by Mr. Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard it -- of it, but I have not read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, some would say that Mr. Izetbegovic was trying to create sort of an Afghanistan a la Taliban in Europe based on what he wrote. Now, setting aside what his political philosophies were, do you think it would be helpful for -- one, for a person drawing a conclusion what if anything Mr. Izetbegovic was promoting in his book, do you think it might have been helpful for them to at least read it first? "Yes," "no," "I don't know". As an intellectual.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't describe myself as intellectual. Yeah, it would be helpful, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay all right and, of course, you've heard the old adage, you can't judge a book by its cover; right?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you could look at 1D 01538.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is a part that we translated, and we're going to go through this, because I think and I hope that the Trial Chamber will pay close scrutiny and attention to what I'm about to say, because I think there is -- even though this was not a policy, no one was subscribing to it, think we at least owe it to Mr. Valenta to be fair and objective about what it is that he had written.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First of all, were you aware that the book was written in 1991 before the war? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew it was written before the war. I didn't know 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the very first page, which wasn't translated, at the very bottom it says: "On the basis of the decision of the Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Physical Culture ..." The very first page of our version, 1D 01538. There is no need to be turning pages. It should be on the very first page, sir. Here, I have an extra copy. Madam Usher. I'm running out of time, that's why.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I need an extra copy. I just need to be orientated to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just look at the first stage.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just need --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First page, bottom, we're going to go through the Prosecution's as well, but this wasn't translated. "On the basis of the decision of the Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Physical Culture - Sarajevo, number 02-413-150, dated 22 August 1991, exempt from paying the sales tax." Question: Were you aware, sir, that there was a law in Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time, that certain texts that were purported to be of a scientific nature or for educational purposes were exempt from taxes, and this book indeed was, at least, exempted from taxes based on a decision made by the Ministry of Education of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Were you aware of that, "yes," "no," "I don't know"?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we -- if I could go to the last -- when -- you were shown photo -- or some maps by the Prosecutor, and you were shown one particular map with all these arrows going from here to there. Did you by any chance look at all the other maps that were in the book to see where they came from and who might have generated those particular maps?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you by any chance look at the book, in the back of the book, to see where the footnotes -- the references to the footnotes, to see who, if anyone, Mr. Valenta was quoting or was referencing his comments to?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was given a brief by Mr. Valenta who said he'd written a book. I didn't make reference to the book. I listened to the brief and saw the maps that he was illustrating his discussion with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Now, in the book, if you read parts of it, and we don't have time, and I want to save time for my colleagues, it is very clear that the book was written at a time prior to the war and as a proposal as one way of preventing a civil war. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I just want to direct your attention -- you can look at the Prosecution's version which is P 00021, and I just want to read one excerpt, which is why I began questioning you about not judging a book by its cover, and which is why I made the comments about Mr. Izetbegovic, and I wasn't subscribing to those views that others may hold about whether he was in his -- a fanatic trying to establish an Afghanistan of a Taliban nature in Bosnia. I was just merely making the point.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you look at page 20. At the very top it says page 60. But at the bottom it says page 20 and it has the other numbers 00311591?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it says here, "I know after the book is published these speculations will be manipulated in a certain way because the theme is unpopular." The theme of the book that is. "The loudest ones will be those who do not read the whole book. I did not want to withhold the idea from a well-intentioned reader that, if necessary, human and civilised resettlement is possible and of mutual interest." Now, two points. In history, we've had legalised resettlements, have we not?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We certainly have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the Treaty of Lausanne, where Greeks were driven from their homes in Asia minor and Turks from Greece went to Turkey, right?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: India and Pakistan --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: India and Pakistan, and you can go on. So there is this concept. But going to the first part, do you think that -- do you allow the possibility that perhaps you might come to a different conclusion about Mr. Valenta and what Mr. Valenta was promoting in his book as an alternative plausible solution to it a civil war which ultimately occurred, do you think at least you owed it to him to first read the book before outright dismissing him as a quack.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't used those terms it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I know you haven't.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I would like to do, sir, i to just give you the context in which I heard this lecture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no, no, I'm not -- I'm not asking you about the lecture. I want you to answer my question, and my question is: Did you read the book? And the answer was no. If --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can object.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I can finish my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to object first because the way in which the question is being formulated is improper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] The witness does not use words like Mr. Valenta is a quack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll reformulate. I'll reformulate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You said he went into one of his exposes says?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in a building --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] No, no --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- at a time when I am witnessing some extremely interesting and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- very challenging times for --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- members of the Croat community --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that's the context in which I form my opinion of a person articulating these views at a time when I am seeing and witnessing movements of people. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- it isn't the cold, quiet reading of a book in a library. It is the context in which I judge Mr. Valenta is important to understand the conclusions I draw.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
